newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - French stocks slip further, German shares jump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French stocks slip further, German shares jump.

text.p: French shares plunged on election jitters to end almost four percent down on Monday but German stocks closed at a record high in thin but volatile trade against the background of market holidays in Britain and the U.S.

The dollar picked up from overnight lows against the mark, testing the 1.69 mark level, and edged higher against the yen. Overall, dealers said, activity in Europe was muted because of the holiday in London.

All eyes were on France, however, where markets caught an early cold after the combined left defied most expectations to outpoll the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of the country's parliamentary election.

Prices later appeared to steady somewhat before Paris blue chips suffered further in mid-afternoon, with the main CAC-40 index showing a loss of more than four percent at one stage. The market later recovered marginally to close 3.91 percent or 108.16 points down.

The franc lost just over half a centime to the mark but ended off overnight lows. Traders and analysts said the modest move in the currency reflected two things -- the first round victory is no guarantee of the final result and few currently believed a Socialist government will renege on France's commitment to European monetary union.

"Really and truly this is still just a case of wait and see," said Richard Hill, head of foreign exchange trading at Bank of America in London. "Any worries that are out there are about the potential to derail EMU."
At 1530 GMT, the mark was trading at 3.3757 francs compared with 3.3698 late on Friday and a high overnight at 3.3773.
Shares in companies the current government plans to privatise but whose future could be affected by a possible left win in the parliamentary election fell sharply on the back of the vote.

Among the biggest losers, defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF slumped on fears a Socialist government might cancel the sale of the state's 58 percent holding and Renault was also badly dented on worries its restructuring plans, entailing job losses, might also be held up.

Dassault Aviation remained suspended with a floor of 1,112 francs, victim of a plunge at the opening due to fears a Socialist administration would effectively nationalise the company by cancelling a planned share sell-off after its planned merger with state-owned Aerospatiale.

"The stock market, putting its trust in opinion polls showing the right would win, had treated the election as a non-event. We are going to pay for it because the market had not taken the political risk fully into account," a dealer said.

"We are faced with the worst possible scenario. Is the right going to return the votes in their favour in the second round? If the left wins, what is going to happen to the Maastricht Treaty? And what about issues such as Thomson," another dealer said.

Meanwhile, German shares, which started a shade weaker, picked up during the day and Frankfurt floor trading closed at a record high, up almost 1.6 percent, helped by gains in chemical shares following news of Swiss drugs giant Roche's takeover of German group Boehringer Mannheim. Wall Street's strong performance on Friday, where the Dow closed up 1.21 percent, was also cited.
The rally continued in post-bourse electronic trade and the IBIS DAX index also ended at an all-time closing high, up 1.31 percent.
STOCK PRICES CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 was closed for a market holiday. On Friday it closed up 10.0 points, or 0.21 percent, at 4,661.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 108.16 points or 3.91 percent at 2,654.74.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 55.67 points at 3657.86.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6899 marks and 116.33 yen compared with 1.6910 marks and 115.49 yen in late European trade on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened steady and was trading in what was described as a slack market at 343.10 in mid-afternoon, slightly up from London's close of 343.05 on Friday. Silver was weaker at 474 cents.
